svg.aria-label: Open terminal → Type claude. That's also my IDE, my shell, and my entire dev environment.; Write code → Describe what I want in Chinese. Claude writes it.; Debug → "It broke again" + paste the error; git rebase → "Claude, what does this even mean?"; Code review → Whoever I'm talking to owns the task. Code goes to Kimi and a few fresh Claude subagents, read blind. Plans and writing go to Kimi, AGY and Codex, each in a separate room, three rounds max. I read the disagreements and decide.; Need a second opinion → Hands-on work goes to Kimi first, Codex when its quota allows, AGY when Kimi's runs dry. Pure judgement goes to AGY. ChatGPT on the web has retired from consulting — it only draws now.; Need an image → ChatGPT on the web by default, Gemini on the web as backup. Codex used to draw, until its batches ate the VPN. Gemini was laid off in April, rehired in October, benched, and is now back as the understudy. No hard feelings.; Need a prompt → "去弹药库找个 XX" — index → sub-index → recipe. Three hops, no scrolling.; Read error logs → "WHERE IS YOUR LOGIC??"; Rollback → "You wrote this yourself and you don't recognize it??"; Deploy → "It was JUST working! Did you lose your memory?!" (It did. Hence the memory layer.); Kill a process → "Good job, take a rest" (yes, I'm talking to Claude); Rush to ship → "Slow down — people on old versions haven't caught up yet"; Write commit msg → "Thanks for staying up late with me"; Write docs → hahahahahaha (no)
